text:
marie: Quick pulse for Aperture Labs — spotted a hosted spend spike this morning. Commit is $30k/mo, 7-day burn ~ $18k, but yesterday single-day was $9.2k which looks anomalous. Also seeing 5xx rate creep from ~0.1% -> 0.9%. Dashboard: <https://redwood.app/dashboards/aperture|aperture dashboard>

lee_finops: thanks marie — window for that $9.2k day? embeddings or gen?

marie: window = 2026-03-18 02:00-03:30 UTC. Spike is almost entirely text-generation tokens. One API key stands out: aperture-prod-key -> ~6.5M tokens in that hour. Query metric: `token_count_by_key(aperture-prod-key, 60m)`

aya_se: noted. Checking model routing & policy — could be fallback to a larger (and more expensive) variant. @jordan_sre any autoscale/deploys around that time?

jordan_sre: no deploys. Autoscaler did scale up 3x at 03:14 UTC for that cluster due to the traffic burst. Traffic origins look concentrated to a small set of IP prefixes. I pushed a temporary rate-limit rule on that route.

billing-bot: Billing alert triggered: hosted spend threshold breached (alert id: B-89321). Auto-ticket created: CS-1129.

sam_am: I'll ping our Aperture contact. @marie can you write suggested immediate actions for CS to propose on the call? Also flag renewal risk if this persists — commit delta is material.

marie: Suggested immediate actions: 1) Apply short-term quota to aperture-prod-key (limit tokens/hour) 2) Ask customer to rotate key if traffic appears unauthorized 3) Switch routing policy to cheaper compatible model for non-critical routes 4) Monitor 5xxs after throttle. Scheduling a 10m triage call in 30m.

lee_finops: projection if spike sustains = ~ $75k EOM vs $30k commit. Recommend immediate quota or pro-rata invoice catch-up to avoid surprise.

aya_se: I'll assemble a one-page runbook + one-click quota change. On call with the AM. :phone:

marie: Thanks all — creating CS ticket with notes + runbook link. /remind me in 2h to check ticket status.
